tasks.title: agents can't see zen-operator on PATH
tasks.task: The operator ships in a versioned publish folder (e.g. builds/release_2/Zen-0.3.4-win-x64) that changes every release. Zen used to add that versioned folder directly to the user PATH, but already-open agent shells never pick up PATH changes, and the entry itself churns on every release. Fix: copy zen-operator's files into the stable AppData/Local/Zen folder (already permanently on PATH via PromptEnvironment.Sync) instead, and clean up the old versioned PATH entry.

requirements.text: SyncOperatorPath copies zen-operator files into the stable AppData/Local/Zen directory
stale versioned PATH entries from older releases are removed

tasks.title: stale global prompt never re-syncs to updated embedded default
tasks.task: PromptEnvironment/SettingsStore only fall back to the embedded default prompt.txt when settings.json's globalPrompt is empty. When a new release ships an improved embedded prompt (as 0.2.8 did), every existing installation keeps serving its old stored globalPrompt forever — prompt.txt on disk gets re-materialized from the stale settings value every launch, so agents on already-onboarded machines never see documentation fixes shipped in later versions. Repro: edit prompt.txt in the repo, ship a build, run it on a machine with a pre-existing settings.json — the on-disk prompt.txt and launched agents still see the old text. Add a way to detect that the stored prompt is an unmodified older version of a previous embedded default and refresh it (e.g. store which embedded-prompt version last matched, or diff against known prior embedded text) without clobbering a user's deliberately customized prompt.

requirements.text: detect when the stored globalPrompt matches a known older embedded default rather than a user customization
refresh settings.json and prompt.txt to the current embedded default in that case
leave a genuinely user-edited prompt untouched

tasks.title: Operator
tasks.task:
The operator is the new single entry point for all tasks to agents (including you) once it is built requests are sent to the operator and it replies with data. 

the operator is a CLI tool. When the program is launched first check the windows 'path' if the operator isnt there OR the path doesnt match update/add it so all agents can freely access it.

when the operator is requested to add data it is added to a queue, then the whole queue is copied, the original queue is cleared, and  the copy is flushed to the json file before being deleted. in requirements i will outline basic jobs of the operator, you will then implement the specific commands.
